newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Two badly injured in Russian building collapse.
newsitem.headline: Two badly injured in Russian building collapse.

text.p: Part of an old five-storey apartment block collapsed in the southern Russian city of Saratov on Monday, starting a fire in which two people were seriously hurt, officials said.

"Two people are in hospital in a critical condition. A 28-year old man has 50 percent burns. He's barely alive. The other victim is poisoned by fumes and is also seriously ill," said a hospital official from Saratov on the Volga river.
An Emergencies Ministry spokeswoman in Moscow said it was not known what caused the collapse but that an explosion had been ruled out.

A local official in Saratov said by telephone that one section of the building had suddenly collapsed at about 11 a.m. (0700 GMT). He did not say how many people lived there and did not speculate what had caused the collapse.

"Information on possible victims and reasons for the collapse is being checked out," said the official, a spokesman at the civil defence headquarters in Saratov, about 750 km (470 miles) southeast of Moscow. Itar-Tass news agency said rescue teams had been rushed to the scene, as well as 10 ambulances.
NTV television said later that all the other people in the building had been evacuated.
